newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares seen slipping more up to Easter.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares seen slipping more up to Easter.

text.p: Danish share prices trickled down on Monday in a market becalmed by the upcoming Easter holiday and an absence already of key players with dealers seeing further falls in thin trade in the coming days.

"A lot of traders have gone on holiday early. There is an acute dearth of sellers or buyers on the market, that is the way things are going to be up to Wednesday evening when the Danish Easter starts," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 1.15 point down at 152.84, while the KFX June future fell 1.40 point to 152.20 with 30 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Top insurer Tryg-Baltica was very much in the limelight after its 1996 result, closing 11 crowns up at 355 after initially soaring eight percent to 372 on a markedly better than expected performance.
Carlsberg shed four crowns to 388 on fears of delays in the British monopoly authorities' approval of the Bass-Carlsberg-Tetley merger deal due to U.K. May elections.
Otherwise FLS Industries put on five crowns to finish at 820 ahead of its 1996 result expected Tuesday.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.262 billion crowns.
